title: Can Playing Music Make Children Smarter?
paragraphs: Listening to a child practice the drums might not be everyone's idea of a fun afternoon — but all that noise could come with some surprising benefits!
A new US study has found that children who play a musical instrument often do better on tests of intelligence, memory, reading and math.

Researchers from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign studied children aged 7 to 9. They looked at 38 children who practiced an instrument for more than 30 minutes a week, and 38 children who didn't have musical training.
The results showed that children who played instruments did better on tests of intelligence and thinking skills.

They also scored higher on tests of working memory. Working memory is what lets you hold information in your mind for a short time while using it to complete a task, such as remembering a phone number while typing it into your phone.
Children with musical training also did better in reading and math.
So does this mean that learning an instrument makes children smarter?

Well, not necessarily. The researchers explained that the study couldn't prove that playing music caused the higher scores. For example, children who learn instruments might also take part in other activities that help them learn.

Also, children who played instruments didn't do better on every test. For example, in one test, children had to draw a line through a difficult path without lifting their pencil. Both groups did about the same.
More research is needed to understand how music and learning are connected. But the next time you hear a child practicing the drums, remember that all that noise might have some benefits!
